text:
maya: heads-up: after the int4 bring-up for asteria-small polyglot (ja/zh/ko/en) we're seeing a small but consistent sacreBLEU drop on ja->en testset. sharing quick notes + samples below.

eval-bot: eval-run finished: ja->en sacreBLEU 28.4 -> 26.1 (baseline int8 28.4, int4 26.1). chrF -0.8. quick diffs follow.

jin: ok. which quant path / converter flags? dynamic/static?

maya: int4 static (q4_0) with per-channel calibration, kernel family=faust_v2. command used: `./run_eval.sh --model asteria-small --quant q4_0 --langs ja-en --split wmt --beam 5`

liam: can you paste a representative diff?

maya: sure — sample source / ref / outputs:

```
SRC: 私は明日京都に行きます。
REF: I am going to Kyoto tomorrow.
BASE: I'm going to Kyoto tomorrow.
INT4: I will go to Kyoto tomorrow .
```

maya: note the extra space before the period in INT4 and slightly different contraction. lots of scores are sensitive to these detok differences.

sara: hmm looks like a detokenization / spacing normalization issue, not necessarily core LM quality. did tokenizer or detok change?

koji: weird — this showed up across JA->EN and some AR->EN RTL cases too? could be a converter-detok interact. can you run tokenize-only on the offending src?

maya: ran tokenize-only on staging tokenizer binary, output:

```
$ ./tokenizer --vocab poly-v3 --input '私は明日京都に行きます。'
tokens (baseline): ['私', 'は', '明日', '京都', 'に', '行き', 'ます', '。']
tokens (int4):     ['私', 'は', '明', '日', '京都', 'に', '行き', 'ます', '。']
```

jin: that split `明日` -> `明` + `日` will shift token indexes and could change attention, alignments, and detok spacing. but tokenizer binaries should be deterministic — why different?

liam: any changes in the conversion pipeline? maybe we accidentally toggled a compatibility mode that adjusts merge rules on export. i remember an experimental flag for legacy detok.

maya: checked artifacts: vocab SHA matches baseline, merges file identical. however the int4 converted shard metadata includes `compat:legacy_detok=1` in the converter header.

eval-bot: artifact audit: asteria-small-int4 conversion run at 1755750001 used converter v0.6.12 with `--legacy-detok` present.

sara: ok that explains spacing + token boundary differences. legacy_detok flips a couple of normalization passes to preserve older detok behavior for ZWJ/emoji; unfortunate side-effect on CJK merging.

koji: @liam did you touch converter defaults in CI?

liam: i added a fallback for a specific ZWJ emoji case in converter to avoid regressions for zh/ja emoji sequences, and enabled `--legacy-detok` experimentally. i didn't expect it to change merging for `明日`. my bad. i'll revert the flag and rebuild the int4 shard.

jin: can we smoke-test a tiny canary before flipping prod? if revert fixes detok, we avoid rollback.

maya: yes please — run canary on small WMT subset (1k samples) and check sacreBLEU/chrF.

liam: estimate 45m to regen shards + push to canary infra. will post job id.

sara: if canary shows improvement, we should: 1) revert converter default, 2) run a tokenizer binary diff test in CI, 3) add a guard in conversion pipeline that flags `legacy_detok` usage for polyglot models.

eval-bot: queued canary re-eval: job=1755777900 (small wmt subset).

maya: thanks — i'll monitor. also saw small RTL token boundary shifts in ar->en that line up with same converter flag. likely same root cause.

koji: short action checklist added to release PR: [verify vocab sha, compare tokenizer binary bytes, check converter flags, run sacreBLEU+chrF, smoke samples in PR].

liam: pushed reverted conversion, canary deployed. linking job when done.

(eval-bot automated follow-up a few hours later): canary result: ja->en sacreBLEU 28.6 (baseline 28.4), chrF +0.3. regression appears resolved.

maya: great — canary looks good. please include the converter flag note in the release notes and add the CI guard. i'll close this thread once PR is merged. PR: https://git.internal.redwood/conv/asteria-int4/pulls/42

sara: adding ticket to prevent future accidental toggles: INF-8276.

maya: thanks everyone. lesson: quant conversion can accidentally change detok knobs — always run tokenizer-only diffs as part of int4 bring-up. :memo:
